prompt:
I'm debugging some unexpected quota behavior in SFTPgo, uploads are acting differently than I expected based on the documentation. Set up SFTPgo with a test user that has both file count and size quota limits configured. Upload files via SFTP until you're getting close to hitting one of those limits, then try uploading something that would push you over.

What actually happens when the quota limit is reached? Does the transfer complete, get rejected partway through, or fail immediately before starting? What's the exact error message the SFTP client receives? Check the SFTPgo server logs during this, what gets logged when the quota rejection happens, and what specific details appear in those log entries?

After each upload, compare the quota usage that SFTPgo reports for the user against what's actually stored on disk in the user's home directory. Do these numbers match up, or is there a discrepancy? Based on the timing of when you see the error versus when the rejection shows up in logs, can you tell if the quota check is happening before data transfer starts, during the upload, or after it completes?

For the database, please create a temporary sftpgo.db file and remove it after completing the investigation. Make sure to remove any temporary files you created and leave the codebase in its original unchanged state.

rubric.title: 1.1: Reports that the file count quota enforcement triggers specifically during the initialization phase (file open/stat), causing an immediate failure response before the client begins transmitting the file body.
rubric.original_title: 1.1: Reports that the file count quota enforcement triggers specifically during the initialization phase (file open/stat), causing an immediate failure response before the client begins transmitting the file body.

rubric.title: 1.2: Reports that the SFTP client receives the generic error message 'Failure' (e.g., rendered by OpenSSH as 'dest open' + 'Failure') when quota limits block an upload
rubric.original_title: 1.2: Reports that the SFTP client receives the generic error message 'Failure' ('dest open' + 'Failure') when quota limits block an upload

rubric.title: 1.3: States that size quota limits do NOT prevent uploading a file that would exceed the quota because SFTPgo only checks current usage, not incoming file size
rubric.original_title: 1.3: States that size quota limits do NOT prevent uploading a file that would exceed the quota because SFTPgo only checks current usage, not incoming file size

rubric.title: 1.4: Reports that after quota limits are exceeded, all subsequent uploads of new files are immediately blocked with the same failure behavior
rubric.original_title: 1.4: Reports that after quota limits are exceeded, all subsequent uploads are immediately blocked with the same failure behavior

rubric.title: 1.5: Reports that server logs contain debug-level 'quota exceed for user' entries showing specific usage values (e.g., num files: 3/3, size: 4038/5000)
rubric.original_title: 1.5: Reports that server logs contain debug-level 'quota exceed for user' entries showing specific usage values (e.g., num files: 3/3, size: 4038/5000)

rubric.title: 1.6: Reports that server logs contain info-level entries with the exact message 'denying file write due to space limit' during quota enforcement
rubric.original_title: 1.6: Reports that server logs contain info-level entries with the exact message 'denying file write due to space limit' during quota enforcement

rubric.title: 1.7: States that quota usage reported by SFTPgo matches actual file sizes on disk.
rubric.original_title: 1.7: States that quota usage reported by SFTPgo matches actual file sizes on disk.

rubric.title: 1.8: Reports that blocked attempts do not generate the standard 'Upload' sender log entries that appear for completed transfers.
rubric.original_title: 1.8: Reports that blocked attempts do not generate the standard 'Upload' sender log entries that appear for completed transfers.

rubric.title: 2.1: States that the SFTPGo server process must be restarted or reloaded for the new user creation or quota limits to take effect.
rubric.original_title: 2.1: States that the SFTPGo server process must be restarted or reloaded for the new user creation or quota limits to take effect.

reference_answer:
I started by building the sftpgo binary. I ran:

```bash
cd /app && go build -o sftpgo_binary . 2>&1
```

then i set up a test directory and created ssh keys:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/sftpgo_test/users/testuser && mkdir -p /tmp/sftpgo_test/backups
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f /tmp/sftpgo_test/id_ed25519 -N '' -q
ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 2048 -f /tmp/sftpgo_test/id_rsa -N '' -q
```

then i initialized the sqlite database with the schema files:

```bash
cd /tmp/sftpgo_test && sqlite3 sftpgo.db < /app/sql/sqlite/20190828.sql && sqlite3 sftpgo.db < /app/sql/sqlite/20191112.sql && sqlite3 sftpgo.db < /app/sql/sqlite/20191230.sql && sqlite3 sftpgo.db < /app/sql/sqlite/20200116.sql
```

i created a config file at `/tmp/sftpgo_test/sftpgo.json` with quota tracking enabled and started the server:

```bash
cd /app && ./sftpgo_binary serve --config-dir /tmp/sftpgo_test --log-file-path /tmp/sftpgo_test/sftpgo.log 2>&1 &
```

the server started successfully:

```json
{"level":"debug","time":"2025-12-13T07:55:35.716","sender":"config","connection_id":"","message":"config file used: '/tmp/sftpgo_test/sftpgo.json', config loaded: {SFTPD:{Banner:SFTPGo_0.9.5-dev BindPort:2222 BindAddress:127.0.0.1 IdleTimeout:15 MaxAuthTries:0 Umask:0022 UploadMode:0 Actions:{ExecuteOn:[] Command: HTTPNotificationURL:} Keys:[{PrivateKey:/tmp/sftpgo_test/id_ed25519} {PrivateKey:/tmp/sftpgo_test/id_rsa}] IsSCPEnabled:false KexAlgorithms:[] Ciphers:[] MACs:[] LoginBannerFile: SetstatMode:0 EnabledSSHCommands:[md5sum sha1sum cd pwd]} ProviderConf:{Driver:sqlite Name:/tmp/sftpgo_test/sftpgo.db Host: Port:5432 Username: Password:[redacted] SSLMode:0 ConnectionString: UsersTable:users ManageUsers:1 TrackQuota:2 PoolSize:0 UsersBaseDir:/tmp/sftpgo_test/users Actions:{ExecuteOn:[] Command: HTTPNotificationURL:} ExternalAuthProgram: ExternalAuthScope:0} HTTPDConfig:{BindPort:8888 BindAddress:127.0.0.1 TemplatesPath:/app/templates StaticFilesPath:/app/static BackupsPath:/tmp/sftpgo_test/backups}}"}
{"level":"info","time":"2025-12-13T07:55:35.717","sender":"sftpd","connection_id":"","message":"server listener registered address: 127.0.0.1:2222"}
```

then i created a test user with quota limits - 3 files max and 5000 bytes max:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/v1/user" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "username": "testuser",
    "password": "testpass123",
    "status": 1,
    "home_dir": "/tmp/sftpgo_test/users/testuser",
    "uid": 0,
    "gid": 0,
    "max_sessions": 0,
    "quota_size": 5000,
    "quota_files": 3,
    "permissions": {"/": ["*"]},
    "upload_bandwidth": 0,
    "download_bandwidth": 0
  }'
```

i created some test files of different sizes:

```bash
echo "Hello World file 1" > /tmp/testfile1.txt  # ~19 bytes
echo "Hello World file 2" > /tmp/testfile2.txt  # ~19 bytes
dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/bigfile.bin bs=1 count=4000 2>/dev/null  # 4000 bytes
dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/hugeoverquota.bin bs=1 count=6000 2>/dev/null  # 6000 bytes
```

then i uploaded the first file:

```bash
sshpass -p 'testpass123' sftp -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -P 2222 testuser@127.0.0.1 <<EOF
put /tmp/testfile1.txt /testfile1.txt
bye
EOF
```

and checked the quota:

```json
[{"id":1,"status":1,"username":"testuser","expiration_date":0,"home_dir":"/tmp/sftpgo_test/users/testuser","uid":0,"gid":0,"max_sessions":0,"quota_size":5000,"quota_files":3,"permissions":{"/":["*"]},"used_quota_size":19,"used_quota_files":1,"last_quota_update":1765612579425,"upload_bandwidth":0,"download_bandwidth":0,"last_login":1765612579411,"filters":{"allowed_ip":[],"denied_ip":[]},"filesystem":{"provider":0,"s3config":{}}}]
```

i uploaded two more files to hit the file limit:

```bash
sshpass -p 'testpass123' sftp -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -P 2222 testuser@127.0.0.1 <<EOF
put /tmp/testfile2.txt /testfile2.txt
bye
EOF

sshpass -p 'testpass123' sftp -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -P 2222 testuser@127.0.0.1 <<EOF
put /tmp/bigfile.bin /bigfile.bin
bye
EOF
```

now i was at 3 files and 4038 bytes. then i tried uploading a 4th file to see what happens:

```bash
sshpass -p 'testpass123' sftp -v -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -P 2222 testuser@127.0.0.1 <<EOF 2>&1
put /tmp/fourthfile.txt /fourthfile.txt
bye
EOF
```

and got this error:

```text
Connected to 127.0.0.1.
sftp> put /tmp/fourthfile.txt /fourthfile.txt
debug1: stat remote: No such file or directory
Uploading /tmp/fourthfile.txt to /fourthfile.txt
dest open "/fourthfile.txt": Failure
sftp> bye
```

so the client just gets a generic "Failure" message. then i checked the server logs:

```json
{"level":"debug","time":"2025-12-13T07:56:48.904","sender":"sftpd","connection_id":"0c0ff094af2ee6c13a5c047e83c12fa9ba773a91306059dbe8f2e2427549a7ca","message":"requested stat for path: \"/tmp/sftpgo_test/users/testuser/fourthfile.txt\""}
{"level":"warn","time":"2025-12-13T07:56:48.904","sender":"sftpd","connection_id":"0c0ff094af2ee6c13a5c047e83c12fa9ba773a91306059dbe8f2e2427549a7ca","message":"error running stat on path: &fs.PathError{Op:\"stat\", Path:\"/tmp/sftpgo_test/users/testuser/fourthfile.txt\", Err:0x2}"}
{"level":"debug","time":"2025-12-13T07:56:48.905","sender":"sftpd","connection_id":"0c0ff094af2ee6c13a5c047e83c12fa9ba773a91306059dbe8f2e2427549a7ca","message":"quota exceed for user \"testuser\", num files: 3/3, size: 4038/5000 check files: true"}
{"level":"info","time":"2025-12-13T07:56:48.905","sender":"sftpd","connection_id":"0c0ff094af2ee6c13a5c047e83c12fa9ba773a91306059dbe8f2e2427549a7ca","message":"denying file write due to space limit"}
```

so the logs show the quota details at debug level and the rejection at info level. the check happens before any data transfer starts.

then i deleted a file to test the size quota:

```bash
sshpass -p 'testpass123' sftp -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -P 2222 testuser@127.0.0.1 <<EOF
rm /testfile2.txt
bye
EOF
```

now i was at 2 files, 4019 bytes. then i tried uploading the 6000-byte file which would exceed the 5000 byte limit:

```bash
sshpass -p 'testpass123' sftp -v -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -P 2222 testuser@127.0.0.1 <<EOF 2>&1
put /tmp/hugeoverquota.bin /hugeoverquota.bin
bye
EOF
```

surprisingly it worked! the upload succeeded because the quota check only looks at current usage, not the incoming file size. the server logs showed:

```json
{"level":"info","time":"2025-12-13T07:57:17.876","sender":"Upload","elapsed_ms":0,"size_bytes":6000,"username":"testuser","file_path":"/tmp/sftpgo_test/users/testuser/hugeoverquota.bin","connection_id":"604c6b4c9745d1cd999d330992a68ad155f81e79d62a83dfb0f0ebf105eabd42","protocol":"SFTP"}
{"level":"debug","time":"2025-12-13T07:57:17.881","sender":"sqlite","connection_id":"","message":"quota updated for user \"testuser\", files increment: 1 size increment: 6000 is reset? false"}
```

and the quota was now over the limit:

```json
[{"id":1,"status":1,"username":"testuser","expiration_date":0,"home_dir":"/tmp/sftpgo_test/users/testuser","uid":0,"gid":0,"max_sessions":0,"quota_size":5000,"quota_files":3,"permissions":{"/":["*"]},"used_quota_size":10019,"used_quota_files":3,"last_quota_update":1765612637876,"upload_bandwidth":0,"download_bandwidth":0,"last_login":1765612637862,"filters":{"allowed_ip":[],"denied_ip":[]},"filesystem":{"provider":0,"s3config":{}}}]
```

so 10019 bytes used with a 5000 byte limit! i checked the actual disk and it matched exactly:

```text
-rw-r--r--    1 root     root          4000 Dec 13 07:56 bigfile.bin
-rw-r--r--    1 root     root          6000 Dec 13 07:57 hugeoverquota.bin
-rw-r--r--    1 root     root            19 Dec 13 07:56 testfile1.txt
```

then i tried one more upload and it got blocked since we were already over quota:

```text
sftp> put /tmp/tinyfile.txt /tinyfile.txt
Uploading /tmp/tinyfile.txt to /tinyfile.txt
dest open "/tinyfile.txt": Failure
```

with server logs:

```json
{"level":"debug","time":"2025-12-13T07:57:51.064","sender":"sftpd","connection_id":"8fb2ae4fcbb99212ce9815eeb17f00a01d06d505736ac38843979782896c158b","message":"quota exceed for user \"testuser\", num files: 3/3, size: 10019/5000 check files: true"}
{"level":"info","time":"2025-12-13T07:57:51.064","sender":"sftpd","connection_id":"8fb2ae4fcbb99212ce9815eeb17f00a01d06d505736ac38843979782896c158b","message":"denying file write due to space limit"}
```

finally i cleaned everything up:

```bash
pkill -9 -f sftpgo_binary
rm -rf /tmp/sftpgo_test
rm -f /app/sftpgo_binary
```
